questions.question: What is the SI unit of universal gravitational constant (G) ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nm²/kg²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)** is a physical constant involved in the calculation of gravitational effects in **Sir Isaac Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**.
 
• According to the law, the **gravitational force (F)** between two bodies is directly proportional to the product of their masses (m1 and m2) and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance (r)** between them: **F = G(m1m2/r²)**.
 
• To find the SI unit of **G**, we rearrange the formula: **G = (F × r²) / (m1 × m2)**.
 
• In the **SI system**, the unit of **force (F)** is the **Newton (N)**, the unit of **distance (r)** is the **meter (m)**, and the unit of **mass (m)** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• Substituting these units into the rearranged formula gives: **Newton × meter² / (kilogram × kilogram)**, which simplifies to **Nm²/kg²** (or **Nm²kg⁻²**). ***Hence, the correct option is Nm²/kg².***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Value of G**: The accepted value of the **Universal Gravitational Constant** is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²**. This value is extremely small, which explains why gravitational forces between everyday objects are not easily noticeable.
 
• **Henry Cavendish**: The first person to accurately measure the value of **G** in a laboratory setting was the English scientist **Henry Cavendish** in the year **1798** using a **torsion balance** experiment.
 
• **Universal Nature**: Unlike the acceleration due to gravity (g), **G** is a **scalar quantity** and is a **universal constant**. This means its value remains the same everywhere in the **universe**, regardless of the medium or the bodies involved.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The dimensional formula for the universal gravitational constant **G** is **[M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between G and g**: It is important to distinguish between **G** (Universal Gravitational Constant) and **g** (Acceleration due to gravity).
 
 
• **G** is constant throughout the universe, while **g** varies from place to place (e.g., **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on **Earth** but about **1.6 m/s²** on the **Moon**).
 
• The relationship between them is given by the formula **g = GM/R²**, where **M** is the mass of the celestial body and **R** is its radius.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Principia**: The concepts of **universal gravitation** were first published by **Isaac Newton** in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
 
• **Weak Force**: Gravity is considered the **weakest** of the **four fundamental forces** of nature (the others being electromagnetism, the strong nuclear force, and the weak nuclear force), yet it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe.

questions.question: In a compound, the elements are combined:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chemically**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **compound** is a **pure substance** formed when **two or more elements** are **chemically combined** in a **fixed proportion** by **mass**. ***Hence, the correct option is chemically.***
 
• The process of forming a **compound** involves **chemical bonding**, where atoms of different elements interact through the **sharing** or **transfer** of **electrons** to achieve stability.
 
• In a **compound**, the constituent **elements** lose their **original physical and chemical properties** and acquire entirely **new properties**. For example, **Sodium (Na)**, a highly reactive metal, and **Chlorine (Cl)**, a toxic gas, combine to form **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, which is common table salt.
 
• The components of a **compound** cannot be separated by **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **hand-picking**, or **evaporation**. They can only be broken down into simpler substances through **chemical reactions** or **electrochemical methods** like **electrolysis**.
 
• The **composition** of a **compound** is always **homogeneous**, meaning every part of the compound has the same **properties** and **composition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Filtration:** This is a **physical separation technique** used to separate an **insoluble solid** from a **liquid** or **gas**. It is applicable to **heterogeneous mixtures** like sand and water. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mixtures:** When elements or substances are combined **physically** without any **chemical bond**, they form a **mixture**. Unlike **compounds**, mixtures retain the properties of their constituents and do not have a **fixed ratio**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation:** This is a **physical process** used to separate a **soluble solid** from its **solvent** (liquid). For example, **common salt** is obtained from **seawater** using this method. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Distillation:** Another **physical method** used to separate components of a **mixture** based on differences in their **boiling points**. It is commonly used to purify **water** or separate **alcohol** from water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions:** Proposed by **Joseph Proust** in **1799**, this law states that a **chemical compound** always contains its component **elements** in a **fixed ratio** by **mass**, regardless of its **source** or **method of preparation**.
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:** Proposed by **John Dalton** in **1803**, it states that if two **elements** form more than one **compound**, the **masses** of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a **ratio of small whole numbers**.
 
• **Energy Change:** The formation of a **compound** is almost always accompanied by an **energy change**, either **exothermic** (releasing heat) or **endothermic** (absorbing heat).
 
• **Common Examples:**
 
 
• **Water (H2O):** Formed by **2 atoms** of **Hydrogen** and **1 atom** of **Oxygen**.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO2):** Formed by **1 atom** of **Carbon** and **2 atoms** of **Oxygen**.
 
• **Methane (CH4):** A primary component of **natural gas**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, a lot of variation in the shape and size of cells makes an organism _______.

more efficient with different cells performing different functions

• **Multicellular organisms** are composed of more than one cell, which allows for a high degree of complexity and **functional specialization**.
 
• The variation in **shape and size** of cells is a direct result of **cell differentiation**. This ensures that cells are structurally adapted to perform specific tasks effectively.
 
• One of the most critical advantages of this variation is the **division of labour**. In a multicellular body, different groups of cells are assigned specific roles such as **digestion, respiration, or nervous coordination**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the phase during which reproductive tissues in humans start maturing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puberty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Puberty** is defined as the period during which the **reproductive tissues** in humans start maturing and the body undergoes various physiological changes to reach **sexual maturity**.
 
• During this phase, the **gonads** (testes in males and ovaries in females) begin to produce **gametes** (sperm and ova) and secrete **sex hormones**.
 
• In girls, puberty generally begins between the **ages of 10 to 14**, whereas in boys, it typically starts between the **ages of 12 to 16**.
 
• The process is initiated by the release of **Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)** from the **hypothalamus**, which subsequently stimulates the **pituitary gland**.
 
• Puberty marks the transition from **childhood** to **adolescence**, making the individual capable of **reproduction**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Puberty.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Menstruation:**
 
 
• It is the periodic shedding of the **uterine lining** (endometrium) and blood through the vagina in females.
 
• The first occurrence of menstruation is called **menarche**, which is a major milestone of **puberty**.
 
• It signifies that the female body has reached a stage where **ovulation** is occurring, but it is a specific biological process within the reproductive cycle rather than the phase of maturation itself.
 
 
 
• **Childhood:**
 
 
• This is the stage of human development from **infancy** until the onset of **puberty**.
 
• During this period, the **reproductive organs** are present but remain in a **dormant or immature state**.
 
• The primary focus of growth during **childhood** is on physical height, weight, motor skills, and cognitive development.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization:**
 
 
• It is the process by which a male **spermatozoon** fuses with a female **ovum** to form a **zygote**.
 
• This event can only take place after **reproductive maturity** has been achieved through **puberty**.
 
• It is a **reproductive event** that leads to pregnancy, not a developmental phase of tissue maturation.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sexual Characteristics:**
 
 
• During **puberty**, humans develop traits that distinguish the sexes but are not directly part of the reproductive system, such as **facial hair** and **deepening of the voice** in males, and **breast development** in females.
 
• These changes are driven by hormones like **testosterone** in males and **estrogen** in females.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The onset of **puberty** is influenced by various factors including **genetics**, **nutrition**, and **environmental conditions**.
 
• The **pituitary gland** plays a master role by secreting **Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)** and **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)**, which signal the **gonads** to begin the maturation process.
 
• In **modern data**, there is a noted trend of earlier onset of **puberty** in many populations, often attributed to improved **nutrition** and health standards.
</ul

questions.question: An object is moving along a straight line with a velocity that is initially positive (+u) and non-zero, but the acceleration is non-uniform and negative, such that the velocity eventually becomes negative (-v) . What does the negative final velocity signify?

options.text: The acceleration became positive at some point.
The object is moving backward relative to its initial direction.
The object has constant but negative acceleration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The object is moving backward relative to its initial direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Velocity** is defined as a **vector quantity**, which means it possesses both **magnitude** (speed) and **direction**. In **one-dimensional motion**, the direction is represented by **positive (+)** and **negative (-)** signs.
 
• When the **initial velocity** is **positive (+u)**, it implies the object is moving in the chosen **reference direction** (often called "forward").
 
• The **acceleration** is stated to be **negative**. When acceleration and velocity have **opposite signs**, the object undergoes **retardation** (slowing down). Because the acceleration remains negative, the object eventually reaches a **velocity of zero**.
 
• After the object momentarily comes to **rest**, the continued **negative acceleration** causes the object to start moving in the **opposite direction**. As it gains speed in this new direction, its **velocity** becomes **negative (-v)**.
 
• A **negative final velocity** signifies that the **direction of motion** has reversed. Therefore, the object is now moving **backward** relative to its **initial direction**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The final velocity **-v** is non-zero; therefore, the object cannot be **at rest** at the end of the described motion. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The transition from a **positive velocity** to a **negative velocity** occurs because of the persistent **negative acceleration**. There is no requirement for the acceleration to become **positive** to achieve a negative velocity. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The problem explicitly mentions that the **acceleration** is **non-uniform**. While the acceleration is negative, its **magnitude** changes over **time**, meaning it is not **constant**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vector vs Scalar**: **Speed** is a **scalar** (always positive or zero), while **velocity** is a **vector**. A change in the sign of velocity always indicates a **180-degree change** in the **direction of motion** in a **straight line**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration**: This occurs when the **velocity** of an object does not change by **equal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**. On a **velocity-time graph**, non-uniform acceleration is represented by a **curve** rather than a straight line.
 
• **Retardation**: This is specifically **negative acceleration** relative to the direction of **velocity**. If an object moves in the **negative direction** and has **negative acceleration**, it actually **speeds up** (accelerates) in the negative direction.
 
• **Reference Frame**: The choice of which direction is **positive** is arbitrary. However, once fixed, all **vectors** like **displacement**, **velocity**, and **acceleration** must follow that **coordinate system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Instantaneous Rest**: At the exact moment the object **changes direction** (switching from +u to -v), its **instantaneous velocity** must be **0**. This is a crucial characteristic of **motion reversal**.
 
• **Real-world Example**: Consider a ball thrown **vertically upward**. The **initial velocity** is **positive** (upward). **Gravity** provides a **negative acceleration** (downward). The ball slows down, stops at the **maximum height**, and then moves **downward** with a **negative velocity**.
 
• **Sign Convention**: In most **physics problems**, rightward or upward is taken as **positive (+)**, while leftward or downward is taken as **negative (-)**.
 
• **Calculus Aspect**: Acceleration is the **derivative of velocity** with respect to **time** (a = dv/dt). If **a** is always **negative**, the **slope** of the **velocity-time graph** is always **downward**, eventually crossing the **time-axis** into the negative region.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following modifications of seeds help in wind dispersal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wing-like or hairy outgrowths**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Wind dispersal**, also known as **Anemochory**, is a method where seeds are carried away from the parent plant by air currents. To facilitate this, seeds develop specific structural modifications.
 
• **Wing-like outgrowths** are found in seeds of plants like **Maple** and **Drumstick**. These wings increase the surface area, allowing the seeds to spin or glide through the air over long distances.
 
• **Hairy outgrowths** are another common modification. Examples include the **hairy seeds** of **Madar (Calotropis)** and the **hairy fruit** of **Sunflower**. These hairs act like tiny parachutes, catching the breeze to keep the seed buoyant.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about kinetic energy?

options.text: It depends on direction of motion.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It depends on direction of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. By definition, any object that is moving has kinetic energy, and if an object is at rest, its kinetic energy is **zero**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Energy is a **scalar quantity**, which means it only has **magnitude** and no **direction**. Unlike velocity or force, which are **vector quantities**, kinetic energy does not require a directional component to be fully described. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is **1/2 mv²**, where **v** is the **speed** (magnitude of velocity). Since the velocity term is **squared**, the **direction of motion** (whether positive or negative, north or south) has no effect on the total energy value. Therefore, it does **not** depend on direction. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Kinetic energy can **never be negative**. This is because **mass (m)** is always a **positive** value, and any real number (velocity) **squared (v²)** results in a **positive** value or **zero**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It depends on direction of motion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathematical Expression:**
 
 
• The standard formula for calculating kinetic energy is **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**.
 
• In this formula, **m** represents the **mass** of the object in **kilograms (kg)** and **v** represents the **velocity** (or speed) in **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**.
 
• One Joule is defined as **1 kg·m²/s²**. In the **CGS system**, the unit is the **erg**, where **1 Joule** equals **10⁷ ergs**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• **Mass**: Kinetic energy is **directly proportional** to the mass of the object. If the mass is **doubled**, the kinetic energy **doubles**.
 
• **Velocity**: Kinetic energy is proportional to the **square of the velocity**. This means if the velocity is **doubled**, the kinetic energy increases **four times** (2 squared).
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Momentum:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy can also be expressed in terms of **linear momentum (p)** using the formula **K.E. = p² / 2m**.
 
• This shows that for a constant mass, kinetic energy increases with the **square of the momentum**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This principle states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. If work is done **on** an object, its speed and kinetic energy increase.
 
• **Types of Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• **Translational Kinetic Energy**: Due to motion from one **location** to another.
 
• **Rotational Kinetic Energy**: Due to an object **spinning** around an axis.
 
• **Vibrational Kinetic Energy**: Due to **vibrational** motion, common in **molecules**.
 
 
 
• **Frame of Reference:** While kinetic energy is a scalar, its **numerical value** depends on the **frame of reference** of the observer. An object may have zero kinetic energy relative to a person sitting next to it, but high kinetic energy relative to an observer on the **ground**.
 
• **Conservation of Energy:** In an **isolated system**, energy can transform between **potential energy** and kinetic energy, but the **total mechanical energy** remains constant in the absence of **friction** or **air resistance**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: A lighter body resists change in motion more strongly.
Inertia of an object increases with its mass.
A body with larger mass has less inertia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inertia of an object increases with its mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia** is defined as the inherent property of an object by virtue of which it resists any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line.
 
• The **Mass** of an object is a quantitative measure of its inertia. This means that **mass** and **inertia** are directly proportional to each other; the more **mass** an object has, the more **inertia** it possesses.
 
• A **lighter body** has less **mass**, which means it offers less resistance to change. Therefore, it is easier to move a stationary lighter object or stop a moving one compared to a heavier one. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Since **mass** is the fundamental property that determines how much an object will resist acceleration, it is the very scale used to measure **inertia**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• When the **mass** of an object is high, the force required to change its velocity is also high. This indicates that the **inertia of an object increases with its mass**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A body with a **larger mass** possesses greater **inertia** because it requires a significantly larger external force to alter its state of motion. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s First Law of Motion:** Often referred to as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**. This law was first formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in his work **Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
 
• **Types of Inertia:**
 
 
• **Inertia of Rest:** The inability of a body to change its state of rest by itself. For example, when a carpet is beaten with a stick, dust particles fall off due to **inertia of rest**.
 
• **Inertia of Motion:** The inability of a body to change its state of uniform motion. For instance, an athlete often runs some distance before taking a **long jump** to gain momentum and utilize **inertia of motion**.
 
• **Inertia of Direction:** The inability of a body to change its direction of motion. An example is when a car takes a sharp turn, the passengers tend to lean **outwards** because their bodies try to maintain the original direction.
 
 
 
• **SI Unit of Mass:** The **kilogram (kg)** is the standard unit used to measure **mass**. In scientific calculations, **inertia** is not measured in a separate unit but is expressed through the magnitude of the **mass**.
 
• **Relationship with Force:** According to **Newton's Second Law**, **Force (F) = mass (m) × acceleration (a)**. This formula highlights that for a constant force, **acceleration** is inversely proportional to **mass**, further proving that higher **mass** (higher **inertia**) results in less change in motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Galileo Galilei** was the first to suggest the concept of **inertia** before **Newton** formalized it. **Galileo** conducted experiments with inclined planes to demonstrate that objects would move forever if **friction** was absent.
 
• It is important to distinguish between **Mass** and **Weight**. While **mass** is a measure of **inertia** and remains constant regardless of location, **weight** is the force of **gravity** acting on that **mass** and changes depending on the **gravitational field** (e.g., Earth vs. Moon).
 
• In a vacuum where **air resistance** is zero, a feather and a hammer will fall at the same **acceleration** due to **gravity**, but the hammer still possesses much higher **inertia** due to its greater **mass**.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of implementing nutrient management practices in agriculture?

options.text: Mixing plastic residues into the field

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Improving crop productivity and quality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nutrient management** refers to the efficient use of **essential plant nutrients** such as **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, and **Potassium (K)** to optimize **crop yield** and minimize environmental impact.
 
• The primary objective of these practices is **Improving crop productivity and quality**. By ensuring plants receive the right amount of nutrients at the right stage of growth, farmers can achieve higher **biological yields** and better **nutritional value**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Enhancing soil erosion** is a negative process that involves the removal of the fertile topsoil layer. Nutrient management, conversely, focuses on maintaining **soil health** and **structure** to prevent such degradation. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pouring polluted water** on crops introduces **heavy metals** and **pathogens** into the **food chain**, which damages crop health and poses risks to human consumption. Nutrient management promotes the use of clean water and specific **irrigation** techniques. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mixing plastic residues** into the field leads to **soil pollution** and disrupts the physical properties of the soil, making it difficult for roots to penetrate and absorb water. Modern agriculture aims for **sustainable waste management** rather than contamination. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Effective nutrient management follows the **4R Stewardship** principle: applying the **Right source**, at the **Right rate**, at the **Right time**, and in the **Right place**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integrated Nutrient Management (INM):** 
 
 
• This approach combines **chemical fertilizers** with **organic manures**, **bio-fertilizers**, and **green manures** to maintain **soil fertility** over the long term.
 
• It helps in reducing the dependency on expensive chemical inputs, thereby lowering **input costs** for farmers while preserving the **ecological balance**.
 
 
 
• **Macro and Micro Nutrients:**
 
 
• Plants require **17 essential elements** for growth. **Macronutrients** like **Carbon**, **Hydrogen**, and **Oxygen** are taken from air and water, while **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Potassium** are the primary minerals supplied via fertilizers.
 
• **Micronutrients** such as **Zinc (Zn)**, **Iron (Fe)**, and **Boron (B)** are needed in smaller quantities but are crucial for enzyme activities and **metabolic functions** in plants.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• Proper management prevents **nutrient leaching** and **surface runoff**, which can lead to **eutrophication** (excessive algal growth) in nearby water bodies.
 
• It also reduces the emission of **greenhouse gases** like **Nitrous Oxide (N2O)**, which is a potent contributor to **global warming**.

__
 
• A **vacuole** is a membrane-bound organelle found in the **cytoplasm** of a cell. While they are present in both animal and plant cells, their size and function differ significantly between the two.
 
• In a **mature plant cell**, the **central vacuole** is a large, prominent sac that typically occupies **50% to 90%** of the total **cell volume**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***

questions.question: If the potential difference between two points is V and charge q moves between them, the work done is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**W = V x q**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electric potential difference** between two points in an electric circuit is defined as the amount of **work done** (**W**) in moving a **unit charge** (**q**) from one point to another.
 
• Mathematically, **potential difference** (**V**) is expressed as the ratio of **work done** to the **charge**, which gives the formula **V = W / q**.
 
• By rearranging this fundamental equation, we find that the **work done** is the product of the **potential difference** and the **charge** moved, represented as **W = V x q**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **electric potential difference** is the **Volt (V)**, named in honor of **Alessandro Volta**, an Italian physicist. One **Volt** is defined as the potential difference between two points when **1 Joule** of **work** is done to move a charge of **1 Coulomb**.
 
• The **work done** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction, and it is measured in **Joules (J)** in the **International System of Units**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Potential**: While **potential difference** is the change in energy between two points, **electric potential** at a single point is the **work done** per unit charge to bring a **positive test charge** from **infinity** to that point.
 
• **Nature of Charge**: The **charge** (**q**) is measured in **Coulombs (C)**. One **Coulomb** is equivalent to the charge of approximately **6.242 x 10^18 electrons**. The **work done** depends linearly on both the magnitude of the charge and the voltage across which it moves.
 
• **Energy Transformation**: In a closed circuit, the **work done** by the **battery** or power source provides the **electrical energy** necessary to move charges through components like resistors or bulbs, where it is converted into **heat** or **light**.
 
• **Relationship with Electric Field**: For a **uniform electric field** (**E**), the **potential difference** (**V**) is also related to the **distance** (**d**) moved by the formula **V = E x d**. Combining this with **W = V x q**, we get **W = F x d**, consistent with the classical definition of work in mechanics.
 
• **Electron-Volt (eV)**: In atomic and nuclear physics, **energy** is often measured in **electron-volts**. **1 eV** is the amount of **kinetic energy** gained by a single **electron** accelerating through a **potential difference** of **1 Volt**, which equals approximately **1.602 x 10^-19 Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direction of Flow**: By convention, **positive charges** move from a point of **higher potential** to **lower potential**. The **work done** by the electric field is positive in this case. If a charge is moved from **lower** to **higher potential**, **external work** must be applied.
 
• **Conservation of Energy**: The formula **W = V x q** is a reflection of the **law of conservation of energy**. The **electrical potential energy** lost or gained by the charge is exactly equal to the **work done** on or by the system.
 
• **Measurement Tools**: A **Voltmeter** is the device used to measure **potential difference**. It is always connected in **parallel** across the points between which the potential difference is to be determined to ensure it measures the **voltage** without significantly altering the **current** in the circuit.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Ohm’s Law?

options.text: It states that resistance decreases with voltage.
It is valid only for metallic conductors at constant temperature.
It is valid for semiconductors and electrolytes.
It is valid for all conductors at all temperatures.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is valid only for metallic conductors at constant temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the **electric current (I)** flowing through a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **potential difference (V)** across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The law specifies that **Resistance (R)** is a constant for a given conductor at a specific temperature. It does not state that resistance decreases with voltage; rather, resistance is the **ratio of V to I**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Ohm's Law is strictly valid for **metallic conductors** (like **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum**) where the relationship between voltage and current is **linear**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• It is not applicable to **non-ohmic conductors** such as **semiconductors** (e.g., **silicon**, **germanium**), **diodes**, **transistors**, and **electrolytes**, as they do not maintain a constant resistance. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The law fails if **temperature** or other physical conditions change, because the resistance of a metal typically increases with an **increase in temperature**. Therefore, it is not valid for all conductors at all temperatures. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin:** The law was named after the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in **1827** in his work "The Galvanic Circuit Investigated Mathematically."
 
• **Mathematical Formula:** It is expressed as **V = I × R**, where **V** is the **Voltage** in **Volts**, **I** is the **Current** in **Amperes**, and **R** is the **Resistance** in **Ohms (Ω)**.
 
• **Resistance Factors:** The resistance of a conductor depends on its **length**, **cross-sectional area**, **nature of the material**, and **temperature**.
 
 
• **Length:** Resistance is **directly proportional** to the length of the conductor.
 
• **Area:** Resistance is **inversely proportional** to the area of the cross-section.
 
 
 
• **Ohmic vs. Non-Ohmic:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:** Conductors that obey Ohm’s Law and show a **straight-line V-I graph** passing through the origin.
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:** Components like **LEDs** and **vacuum tubes** where the V-I graph is **curved**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations:** Ohm’s Law is not a universal law of nature (like the law of gravity) but rather an empirical description of the behavior of certain materials.
 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** When a high current passes through a wire, it produces **heat** (Joule heating). This rise in temperature increases the **vibrations of atoms**, which leads to more collisions with electrons, thereby **increasing resistance** and causing a deviation from Ohm's Law.
 
• **Applications:** It is used to determine the **voltage**, **resistance**, or **current** of an electric circuit. It also helps in choosing the correct **fuses** and **circuit breakers** for household appliances.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of liquids?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liquids are a state of matter characterized by having a **definite volume** but **no fixed shape**. This means that if you pour **500 ml** of water from a glass into a bowl, the volume remains **500 ml**, but the water takes the shape of the bowl.
 
• The particles in a **liquid** are close to each other but not as tightly packed as in **solids**. This arrangement allows the particles to slide past one another, providing the property of **fluidity**.
 
• Because the particles have some **kinetic energy** and are not held in a rigid lattice, liquids can flow and change their **physical form** based on the **container** they are placed in. ***Hence, the statement "No fixed shape but fixed volume" is correct.***
 
• The **intermolecular forces of attraction** in liquids are strong enough to keep the particles together (maintaining volume) but not strong enough to fix them in specific positions (resulting in no fixed shape).
 
• Compared to **gases**, liquids have much higher **density** and are relatively **incompressible** because there is very little empty space between the individual molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solid State:**
 
 
• **Solids** have both a **fixed shape and a fixed volume**. The particles are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern called a **crystal lattice**.
 
• The **intermolecular forces** are extremely strong, meaning the particles only **vibrate** around fixed positions and cannot move freely.
 
 
 
• **Gaseous State:**
 
 
• **Gases** have **no fixed shape and no fixed volume**. They expand to fill the entire space of whatever **container** they are in.
 
• The particles in a gas have high **kinetic energy** and are separated by large distances, making gases highly **compressible**.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion:**
 
 
• Liquids undergo **diffusion**, where particles mix with other substances. This process is faster than in **solids** but slower than in **gases**. For example, adding a drop of **ink** to **water** demonstrates the diffusion of liquid particles.
 
 
 
• **Surface Tension and Viscosity:**
 
 
• **Surface Tension** is a property of liquids where the surface molecules are pulled inward, causing the surface to behave like a **thin elastic skin**.
 
• **Viscosity** is the measure of a liquid's **resistance to flow**. For example, **honey** has a higher viscosity than **water** because its particles have stronger internal friction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **boiling point** is the **temperature** at which a liquid turns into a gas at a specific **atmospheric pressure**.
 
• The **freezing point** is the **temperature** at which a liquid changes into a **solid** as **energy** is removed.
 
• While most substances are denser in their solid state, **water** is a unique example where the **solid (ice)** is less dense than the **liquid**, which is why ice floats.
 
• The **kinetic theory of matter** explains that the state of a substance (solid, liquid, or gas) depends on the **temperature** and **pressure** applied to it.
</ul

• **Statement A** mentions its use in **soaps and paper**. In the **soap industry**, it is a fundamental ingredient used in **saponification**, a chemical reaction where it reacts with fats and oils to produce soap.
 
• In the **pulp and paper industry**, **sodium hydroxide** is used to treat wood pulp. It helps in dissolving **lignin**, the substance that binds wood fibers together, thereby facilitating the creation of high-quality white paper. *Hence, statement A is correct.*
 
• **Statement B** claims it is a **weak base** and **neutral** in nature. In chemistry, a **base** is classified based on its degree of ionization. **Sodium hydroxide** is a **strong base** because it dissociates completely into **sodium ions (Na+)** and **hydroxide ions (OH-)** in an aqueous solution.
 
• The **pH scale** measures how acidic or basic a substance is, ranging from **0 to 14**. A **neutral** substance has a **pH of 7**. However, a concentrated solution of **sodium hydroxide** has a **pH value** of approximately **14**, making it extremely **alkaline** rather than neutral. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*

• **Strong vs. Weak Bases:**
 
 
• **Strong Bases:** Examples include **NaOH** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**. They fully ionize in water.
 
• **Weak Bases:** Examples include **Ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH)** and **Magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)2)**. They do not fully ionize and maintain a lower concentration of **hydroxide ions**.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**

• When a **non-metallic oxide** reacts with a **strong base**, a **neutralization reaction** takes place, producing **salt** and **water**.
 
• In this specific reaction, the acidic oxide behaves like a **weak acid**. When a **weak acid** reacts with a **strong base**, the resulting salt is **Basic** in nature. ***Hence, the statement regarding the basic nature of the salt is correct.***
 
• The **pH** of the salt solution formed in this process is **greater than 7**. This is because the **anion** of the salt (derived from the weak acid) undergoes **hydrolysis** in water, releasing **hydroxide ions (OH-)**, which makes the solution **alkaline**.
 
• A classic example of this reaction is **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** reacting with **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, a **strong base**, to form **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3)** and water. **Sodium Carbonate** is a well-known **basic salt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Oxides:**
 
 
• **Metallic Oxides:** Most metals react with oxygen to form **basic oxides** (e.g., **MgO**, **Na2O**). These oxides react with acids to form salt and water.
 
• **Non-Metallic Oxides:** These are **acidic** (e.g., **SO2**, **NO2**) or **neutral** (e.g., **CO**, **N2O**). Acidic non-metallic oxides react with bases to form salts.
 
• **Amphoteric Oxides:** Some oxides show both acidic and basic properties, such as **Aluminium Oxide (Al2O3)** and **Zinc Oxide (ZnO)**.
 
 
 
• **The pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is considered **neutral** (like pure water at **25°C**).
 
• Solutions with a **pH less than 7** are **acidic**, while those with a **pH greater than 7** are **basic** or **alkaline**.
 
• The nature of a salt depends on the strength of the parent **acid** and **base** used during its formation.
 
 
 
• **Strong Bases:**
 
 
• A **strong base** is a compound that completely dissociates into its ions in an aqueous solution. Common examples include **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** and **Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• These substances have high **pH values**, typically ranging from **12 to 14** in concentrated forms.
 
 
 
• **Types of Salts:**
 
 
• **Neutral Salts:** Formed from a **strong acid** and a **strong base** (e.g., **NaCl**).
 
• **Acidic Salts:** Formed from a **strong acid** and a **weak base** (e.g., **NH4Cl**).
 
• **Basic Salts:** Formed from a **weak acid** and a **strong base** (e.g., **CH3COONa**, **Na2CO3**).

questions.question: When onion bulbs of different sizes are viewed under a microscope, all show similar rectangular structures. This proves that _________.

options.text: all living things are made of cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**all living things are made of cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When observing an **onion peel** under a **compound microscope**, the basic structures look the same regardless of whether the **onion bulb** is small, medium, or large.
 
• These small, repeating **rectangular structures** are the **fundamental building blocks** of the onion bulb, and they are known as **cells**.
 
• The fact that different sizes of the same organism show the same **cellular structure** proves that the **cell** is the **structural unit** of life, supporting the conclusion that **all living things are made of cells**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Individual **cells** in an onion do not significantly differ in their basic architecture because they belong to the same **species** (**Allium cepa**) and **tissue type** (**epidermal tissue**). ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The presence of **cells** is a universal characteristic of all living organisms, not just large ones. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **cork cells** were the first cells discovered, they are dead cells; **onion peel cells** observed in fresh bulbs are **living cells** containing **protoplasm**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cell Theory:** This is a landmark theory in biology formulated by **Matthias Schleiden** (a **German botanist**) in **1838** and **Theodor Schwann** (a **German zoologist**) in **1839**. It states that all **plants** and **animals** are composed of **cells**.
 
• **Onion Cell Features:** **Onion cells** are typical **plant cells**. They possess a rigid **cell wall** made of **cellulose**, a **nucleus** pushed to the periphery, a large central **vacuole**, and **cytoplasm**.
 
• **Microscopic Observation:** To view these **cells**, a thin layer of **epidermis** is removed from the fleshy **leaf** of the **onion**, placed on a **glass slide**, and stained with **Safranin** or **Iodine solution** to highlight the **nucleus** and **cell walls**.
 
• **Function of the Cell Wall:** The distinct **rectangular shape** seen under the **microscope** is due to the **cell wall**, which provides **mechanical strength** and **protection** to the plant cell.
 
• **Magnification:** These structures are typically observed under low power (**10x**) and then high power (**40x**) objectives of a **light microscope**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Cells:** **Robert Hooke** discovered the **cell** in the year **1665**. He observed a thin slice of **cork** and noticed structures resembling a **honeycomb** or "little rooms."
 
• **Living Cells:** **Anton van Leeuwenhoek**, in **1674**, used an improved **microscope** to discover free-living **cells** (like **bacteria** and **protozoa**) in pond water for the first time.
 
• **Discovery of Nucleus:** The **nucleus**, which acts as the control center of the **cell**, was discovered by **Robert Brown** in **1831**.
 
• **Expansion of Cell Theory:** In **1855**, **Rudolf Virchow** refined the **Cell Theory** by stating "**Omnis cellula-e cellula**," meaning all **cells** arise from **pre-existing cells**.
 
• **Protoplasm:** The term **protoplasm** for the fluid substance of the **cell** was coined by **Purkinje** in **1839**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastic bag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-biodegradable materials** are substances that cannot be broken down or decomposed by **biological processes** or **microorganisms** such as **bacteria** and **fungi**.
 
• **Plastic bags** are manufactured from **synthetic polymers** like **high-density polyethylene (HDPE)**. These materials possess strong **chemical bonds** that are not recognized by the enzymes of **decomposers**, making them persist in the **environment** for **hundreds of years**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Paper** is primarily composed of **cellulose**, which is an **organic compound** derived from **plants**. It is easily digested by **microbes** and typically decomposes within **2 to 6 weeks** under appropriate conditions of **moisture** and **temperature**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Vegetable peels** are classified as **wet waste** or **organic matter**. They are highly **biodegradable** and can be converted into **compost** or **organic manure** through **natural decomposition** within a few **days** or **weeks**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cotton cloth** is made from **natural fibers** obtained from the **cotton plant**. Being a **plant-based product**, it is **biodegradable** and generally takes about **2 to 5 months** to decompose in the **soil**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Waste:**
 
 
• **Biodegradable waste:** Includes **food waste**, **agricultural residues**, **wood**, and **paper**. These can be processed via **vermicomposting** or **anaerobic digestion** to produce **biogas**.
 
• **Non-biodegradable waste:** Includes **glass**, **metals**, **plastics**, and **synthetic chemicals**. These materials require **recycling** or **safe disposal** in **landfills** to prevent **environmental pollution**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Plastic Pollution:**
 
 
• Plastics undergo **photodegradation**, where **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** from the **sun** breaks them into smaller fragments called **microplastics** (less than **5mm** in size).
 
• These **microplastics** enter the **food chain** through **aquatic ecosystems**, leading to **bioaccumulation** and potential **health hazards** for **humans** and **wildlife**.
 
 
 
• **Global and National Regulations:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** notified the **Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021**, which prohibited the manufacture, import, and sale of identified **single-use plastic (SUP)** items with effect from **July 1, 2022**.
 
• The **United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA)** has also proposed a global treaty to end **plastic pollution**, emphasizing the **circular economy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decomposition Timeframes:** While **organic waste** like **banana peels** takes about **1-2 weeks**, **aluminum cans** can take **80-200 years**, and **glass bottles** may take **1 million years** to degrade.
 
• **The 5 R’s Principle:** To manage **non-biodegradable** waste effectively, the hierarchy followed is **Refuse**, **Reduce**, **Reuse**, **Repurpose**, and **Recycle**.
 
• **Leaching:** **Non-biodegradable** materials in **landfills** can cause **leaching**, where **toxic chemicals** seep into the **groundwater**, affecting **water quality** and **soil fertility**.
 
• **Energy Recovery:** Some **non-biodegradable** wastes with high **calorific value** are used in **Waste-to-Energy (WtE)** plants to generate **electricity** through **incineration**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about neutrons is correct?

options.text: They revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits.
They determine the chemical properties of an atom.
They are found in the nucleus of an atom.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are found in the nucleus of an atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neutrons** are subatomic particles that, along with **protons**, are located in the **nucleus** of an atom. They were discovered by the British physicist **James Chadwick** in the year **1932**.
 
• Statement 1 suggests that they revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits. This is inaccurate as it describes the behavior of **electrons**, which occupy the space around the nucleus in **shells** or **orbitals**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 claims they determine chemical properties. While neutrons affect the **mass** and stability of an atom, the **chemical properties** are primarily determined by the number and arrangement of **electrons** in the outermost shell. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3 asserts they are found in the nucleus. Neutrons and protons are collectively known as **nucleons** and are held together in the **central core** of the atom by the **strong nuclear force**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 4 mentions they have a positive charge. In reality, **protons** carry a **positive charge (+1)**, while neutrons have **no electric charge** (neutral). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The number of neutrons in an atom can vary, leading to different **isotopes** of the same element, such as **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass of Neutron:** The mass of a neutron is approximately **1.6749 x 10^-27 kg**, which is slightly greater than the mass of a **proton** (**1.6726 x 10^-27 kg**). In atomic mass units, it is roughly **1.00866 amu**.
 
• **Role in Nuclear Fission:** Neutrons play a critical role in **nuclear chain reactions**. In **nuclear reactors**, slow-moving or **thermal neutrons** are used to bombard heavy nuclei like **Uranium-235** to trigger **fission**.
 
• **Beta Decay:** Outside the nucleus, a free neutron is unstable and has a **mean lifetime** of about **880 seconds** (nearly **14 minutes and 40 seconds**). It decays into a **proton**, an **electron**, and an **electron antineutrino**.
 
• **Isotopes:** Atoms of the same element that have the same number of **protons** but different numbers of **neutrons** are called **isotopes**. For example, **Deuterium** is a hydrogen isotope with **one neutron**, whereas ordinary hydrogen (**Protium**) has **zero neutrons**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery Context:** **James Chadwick** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935** for the discovery of the neutron, which proved that the atomic nucleus contained more than just protons.
 
• **Atomic Mass Number:** The **Mass Number (A)** of an atom is the sum of the number of **protons (Z)** and the number of **neutrons (N)**. Therefore, **N = A - Z**.
 
• **Neutrality:** Because neutrons are **electrically neutral**, they can penetrate deep into materials and atoms without being repelled by the **electrostatic forces** of the nucleus or electrons, making them ideal for **neutron diffraction** studies.
 
• **Stability:** The ratio of **neutrons to protons (N/Z ratio)** is a key factor in determining the **nuclear stability** of an element. If this ratio is too high or too low, the nucleus becomes **radioactive**.
</ul
